notes:
Quick CRM notes and summary: Frostbyte builds an IDE-native copilot aimed at enterprise dev teams. Primary ask: deterministic, reproducible code completions across model updates so customers can reproduce CI runs and audit changes. They insist on model/version pinning with immutable artifacts (model hash) exposed in responses and rollbacks that are fast. Low-latency streaming for character-by-character completion (target <50ms median), and ability to run canary rollouts by user segment (internal beta vs org-wide). Also want eval gates integrated into rollout pipeline: hold traffic to new version until pass on predetermined prompt/eval sets (unit-level code snippets, repo-based regression tests).

Important technical points from SE call: they use persistent KV cache in the copilot session; want guidance on cache invalidation across model upgrades. Concerned about subtle tokenization and sampling differences causing non-reproducible completions even when using same model family/version — asking for reproducibility SLOs and tooling to diff token-level outputs. Cost sensitivity moderate — majority of customers expect predictable per-completion pricing. Security: SSO + audit logs + KMS key control mandatory for enterprise customers; some EMEA customers need data residency in eu-west.

Quotes: "We need a guarantee that our CI won't flip because of a model tweak—if it does, we need a meaningful diff and rollback path." — Frostbyte CTO. POC goals: 1) prove pinned model v0.9.3 reproduces baseline completions on 10k prompts, 2) demonstrate canary rollout and automated eval gate, 3) show telemetry for token-level variance and latency breakdown per-token.
